gaps.sentence: The book gives a detailed ___ account of the period.
gaps.hint: connected with the study of the past
gaps.explanation: 'Historical' means relating to history or the past; 'historic' means important in history.

gaps.sentence: She gave me some useful ___ about buying a house.
gaps.hint: a noun is needed after 'some useful'
gaps.explanation: 'Advice' is the uncountable noun; 'advise' is the verb. 'Advices' is not standard English.

gaps.sentence: She studied ___ for her final exams.
gaps.hint: adverb meaning with a lot of effort
gaps.explanation: 'Hard' is an adverb meaning with great effort ('work hard'); 'hardly' means almost not at all.

gaps.sentence: Tax is calculated on your total annual ___.
gaps.hint: all the money you receive from every source
gaps.explanation: 'Income' is all the money you receive from work, investments, rent and so on during a period.

gaps.sentence: The ___ of repairing the roof was higher than we expected.
gaps.hint: the amount of money needed to do something
gaps.explanation: 'The cost of doing something' is the money needed to do it; 'price' is asked for goods, not activities.
'Valuable' means worth a lot of money; 'valued' means appreciated; 'invaluable' already means priceless, so it is not graded.

gaps.sentence: Thousands of people were forced to ___ their homes.
gaps.hint: a verb is needed after 'to'; meaning: abandon
gaps.explanation: 'Desert' is also a verb meaning to abandon; 'dessert' is only the sweet course of a meal.

gaps.sentence: Our team has a good ___ of winning on Saturday.
gaps.hint: pattern: have a good ___ of doing something
gaps.explanation: 'Have a chance of doing something' is the standard collocation for the likelihood of success.
